symptom: (7) LVS mismatch: missing, shorted, or open nets

first_checks.check: Confirm the LVS run compared the intended source-netlist revision against the current routed database (no stale netlist, no stale runset).
first_checks.why_first: cheapest; a stale source explains wholesale missing/extra nets and saves hours

first_checks.check: Read the LVS mismatch header: is it 'net missing in layout/source', 'short', or 'open (net split)', and are PG/well/global nets implicated?
first_checks.why_first: rules out the most severe class; PG/global shorts and opens are systematic, not random local defects

first_checks.check: Check whether every instance of a repeated cell/library cell shows the same net problem, or only one instance.
first_checks.why_first: a repeated hit points to the cell view, fill, or DECAP, not random routing

first_checks.check: Check if the suspect net has a real driver and load in the source, or is a floating/tie-off/unused net.
first_checks.why_first: cheapest way to see if a 'missing net' is harmless/unused rather than a defect

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Re-run LVS with a different partitioning seed and with one specific parallel extraction partition excluded from the merge (or run flat/non-partitioned).
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: short/open vanishes when that partition is dropped or with a different seed: merge/partition artifact, not a real defect
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: discrepancy persists in every seed/partition and in a flat run: merge artifact excluded; the net is genuinely shorted or open in the layout

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Trace the suspect net's extracted connectivity while ignoring net names/labels: check whether the metal is physically continuous versus whether the two pieces simply carry different or missing text labels.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: metal is continuous but the pieces have different/missing labels: the 'open' is a net-naming/label-omission artifact, not a real disconnection
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: metal is physically disjoint (no connecting via/overlap): labeling artifact excluded; it is a real open (missing via or broken route)

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Re-run extraction/LVS with dummy metal fill, DECAP, and filler cells excluded or black-boxed from the comparison.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: short disappears when fill/filler is ignored: the bridge is caused by dummy/fill geometry or an extraction rule merging fill into the net (phantom short)
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: short persists with fill/filler excluded: fill-induced phantom short excluded; it is a real route bridge or device/contact short in intentional wiring

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Cross-probe the missing net in the source: identify its driver and loads and whether the layout has the corresponding devices/placement.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: net has no real driver/load in layout (tie-off, unconnected input, or instance never placed/ECO'd): source/intent mismatch or ECO omission, not an extraction defect
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: the net drives real loads present in layout but is absent from extraction: intent mismatch excluded; it is a missing route/label or extraction problem in the layout

common_root_causes.cause: Real open: missing via/contact or a route that failed to connect (e.g., ECO re-route broke an existing net).
Real short: unintended bridge in routing or metal sliver/dummy-fill bridging two nets.
Missing or misplaced net label (text) causing LVS to split one net into unnamed pieces (reported as open/missing).
Stale/mismatched source netlist or un-back-annotated ECO (net exists in one, not the other).
Distributed-LVS partition/merge artifact (phantom short or open at a partition boundary) or bad via recognition in the runset.

classic_trap: Assuming a reported 'open' or 'short' is a physical route defect and re-routing/patching the layout, when it is actually a missing net label or a partition-merge artifact — or the mirror: quieting the error by adding a label/tie-off instead of fixing the real missing via or bridge.
node_era_note: At 7nm-and-below, multi-patterning coloring errors, cut-mask/via-pillar extraction, and fill/dummy-induced or partition-merge phantom nets dominate, whereas at 28nm most opens/shorts are straightforward missing-via or route-bridge defects.

symptom: (8) LVS mismatch: wrong device sizes or extra devices

first_checks.check: Read the device-mismatch summary: is it 'extra device in layout', 'missing device in layout', or a property mismatch (W/L/M/fingers) on a matched device?
first_checks.why_first: cheapest; separates count mismatch from size/parameter mismatch, which have disjoint cause sets

first_checks.check: Check whether the implicated devices are physical-only cells (tap, endcap, filler, DECAP, antenna diode) and whether the runset black-boxes/ignores them.
first_checks.why_first: rules out the most common systematic cause of extra devices; prevents debugging filler as logic

first_checks.check: Compare the magnitude of the size delta: tiny sub-1%/rounding difference versus an integer or ratio mismatch (2x W, different finger count, M-factor).
first_checks.why_first: rounding deltas are measurement convention; ratio mismatches are real parameter/Pcell errors

first_checks.check: Confirm the source netlist is the post-route/back-annotated version (not pre-place/pre-optimization) and check for ECO/P&R insertions (buffer, gate sizing).
first_checks.why_first: stale netlist explains wholesale wrong sizes/extra devices and is cheap to verify

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Re-run LVS with physical-only cells (filler, decap, tap, endcap, antenna diode) explicitly black-boxed/ignored.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: extra-device count drops to zero and remaining devices match: the extras were unmarked physical-only cells (runset/ignore-setup issue), not real logic
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: extras persist as named logic instances: physical-only-cell artifact excluded; there is a genuine extra instance in layout (or a device missing from the source)

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Toggle LVS parallel-transistor/finger merging (or compare extracted multiplicity) and re-run.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: size/count mismatch disappears when fingers are merged (or not merged): it is a fingering/multiplicity counting convention between netlist and layout, not a drawn-size error
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: mismatch is invariant to the merge setting: fingering convention excluded; the W/L/M or device count really differs

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Measure the drawn geometry (poly width / number of fins) of the suspect device in the layout and compare it to the netlist parameter (times any bias/quantization).
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: drawn geometry matches the netlist parameter within rounding/quantization, yet LVS reports a different value: it is a drawn-vs-effective measurement or rounding/unit convention, not a real sizing error
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: drawn geometry is grossly different from the netlist parameter: rounding/measurement artifact excluded; the device is really drawn at the wrong size (Pcell parameter or manual edit)

discriminating_experiments.experiment: For an extra device with no source counterpart, inspect its connectivity: are all terminals tied to the same net/floating, or is it a scan/DFT/leftover ECO instance?
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: terminals are shorted/floating or it is a DFT/scan physical leftover: it is an unused/leftover instance that can be black-boxed, or the netlist is missing a physical-only view
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: the device is properly connected and drives logic: leftover/physical-only excluded; the source netlist is genuinely missing a device (incomplete netlist or failed ECO back-annotation)

common_root_causes.cause: Physical-only cells (filler, decap, tap, endcap, antenna diode) in layout but not in netlist / not black-boxed in runset, reported as extra devices.
Stale source netlist or P&R optimization (gate sizing, buffer insertion, Vt swap) not back-annotated, giving wrong W/L/M or extra/missing devices.
Fingering / multiplicity convention mismatch: netlist says one device with N fingers or M=N, layout extracted as N parallel (or one wide) device.
Drawn-vs-effective parameter rounding or unit/measurement convention (sub-nm width rounding, gate-length bias, diffusion-shared W) giving tiny 'wrong size' deltas.
Leftover, duplicate, or DFT/scan-inserted instance in layout (ECO not removed, or partition-merge duplicate) creating a real extra device.

classic_trap: The classic trap is editing the netlist (or waiving) to make an 'extra device' go away when the extras are physical-only cells the runset forgot to black-box; and for 'wrong size', changing the drawn W/L to match the netlist when the delta is just drawn-vs-effective rounding or finger counting — or conversely, waiving a gross 2x ratio as 'rounding'.
node_era_note: At 7nm-and-below, 'size' is quantized fin count (no continuous W) so size/extra mismatches are mostly fin-count/fin-cut Pcell quantization and standard-cell dummy/filler, whereas at 28nm planar, size mismatches are continuous drawn-W/effective-W rounding and gate-length bias.
